subject: Human Body
title: How Proteins Get Broken Down
description: A quick win: understand How Proteins Get Broken Down.

hook.text: A steak entering your stomach is a tightly wound chain of proteins. Acid unravels it within minutes.

buildup.text: Pepsinogen, an inactive enzyme, is released by chief cells. Stomach acid converts it to active pepsin.

discovery.text: Pepsin snips protein chains into shorter peptides. These fragments move to the small intestine for final breakdown.

twist.text: Pepsin only works in acidic conditions. If you neutralize stomach acid, protein digestion slows dramatically.

climax.text: The stomach's acid-and-enzyme duo is specialized for protein. Fats and carbs mostly pass through for later work.

punchline.text: The stomach's specialty is protein. Everything else waits.
